clearedSpotChecks.check: World Chain parent-storage replay: the transaction(s) whose PoolManager part was not reproduced (0xd95f40ab59e7bca648d755b43ddcc251f6bff46ca3c2533e67b6d9c8d624959e).
clearedSpotChecks.note: eth_getTransactionByHash and eth_getTransactionReceipt on https://worldchain-mainnet.g.alchemy.com/public confirm block 0x2467a02 (38173186), index 6, from 0xec1423b0... to 0x4527f63f..., status 1, input starting 0x00000001. On chain the transaction made two PoolManager swaps, so the reference never compared the PoolManager part of this transaction; the entry says that correctly. I checked the mined flows by hand instead. Swap 1 (pool 0x8f48dafa..., fee 70000) has amount0 -24451193092485 and amount1 7434149380129393199126, and token 0xf4310b26 sends exactly 7434149380129393199126 from the PoolManager to the caller. Swap 2 (pool 0x9370471b..., fee 100) has amount0 1107404874614473460565423 and amount1 -7434149380129393199126. Token 0xe5bb09bb sends 1107404874614473460565423 from the PoolManager to the caller, and the caller sends 7434149380129393199126 of 0xf4310b26 back to the PoolManager. The native leg also matches: the WETH Withdrawal is 39773443096034, the WETH sent onward is 15322250003549, and the difference is 24451193092485, the amount0 of swap 1. Every PoolManager credit and debit in the receipt equals a Swap delta to the unit. Nothing in the transaction points to a PoolManager fault. The math of the two swaps against pool state was not checked, because the block prestate depends on the earlier ERC-4337 bundle at index 1.

clearedSpotChecks.check: L-1044 Task 1 and 4 on X Layer: word by word replay of mined PoolManager transactions from their own prestate traces, including the 1448 zero gas price transactions of the window.
clearedSpotChecks.note: eth_getTransactionByHash on https://rpc.xlayer.tech for 0xaaa53cd1298f91a22519e9fd0758fae6efba0d7ad286a12f957c0cb6918a14e5 (from raw/196/txmeta.json) returns type 0x2 with gasPrice, maxFeePerGas and maxPriorityFeePerGas all 0x0, to 0x7c5bee2a8091c3ef39072f64f18fac913060aeaf. The receipt has status 1 and effectiveGasPrice 0x0, and it contains a PoolManager Swap log from 0x360e68fa.... That confirms that a whitelisted contract reaches the PoolManager at zero gas price. I reran scripts/model.py myself on the stored trace raw/196/tx/0xaaa53cd1....json.gz: 17 words compared, 0 mismatches (unlock, sync, settle, swap of one step, take). To check that the comparator works, I flipped one bit of one PoolManager post-state storage word and reran. The comparator reported exactly that slot as a storage mismatch. Zero gas price changes only the cost of sending calls. It does not change what the PoolManager computes, and the open medium lead on who can use the whitelist is the right follow-up.

clearedSpotChecks.note: eth_getTransactionByHash on https://rpc.mainnet.tempo.xyz for 0xafaed6cea9e20d404f33a3cd25472135b3bba928d2e565d04a09d78a932f2f2c returns type 0x76 and feeToken 0x20c0...6a37da5c996874be. It carries four calls: approve on that token, a call to 0xdec0... (the DEX), approve on 0x20c0...0000, and a router call to 0x5567954c.... In the receipt (status 1) the PoolManager 0x33620f62... emits one Swap. It receives 900000 of 0x20c0...0000 and sends 899998 of 0x20c0...b9537d11c60e8b50. The transaction fee of 201 units of the fee token goes from 0x58aa7ce4... to 0xfeec0000.... So the fee is charged to the payer and not to the PoolManager balance. I reran scripts/model.py on the stored traces of this transaction and of 0x0602b6154e9ac0c3df327b0ea6ff1545efceb3281d2502586c0f7983e6137427 (type 0x76 with four calls, a swap of more than one step). They compared 15 and 20 words with 0 mismatches. That agrees with the entry.
